definition: The electrode where oxidation takes place. It is negative in a voltaic cell and positive in an electrolytic cell.
The electrode where reduction takes place. It is positive in a voltaic cell and negative in an electrolytic cell.

A tube or strip of filter paper holding a solution of an unreactive salt, such as potassium nitrate, that joins two half-cells. Its ions move between them to keep each solution electrically neutral, so the current keeps flowing.
An electrochemical cell that converts the energy of a spontaneous redox reaction into electrical energy. A primary cell is used until its reactants run out and cannot be recharged.
A rechargeable cell: a spontaneous redox reaction produces electrical energy on discharge, and an external electrical supply reverses that reaction to recharge it.
